task_instance: Apply the skill's server-management principles to a concrete scenario: take a small Node.js HTTP service and manage it the way the skill prescribes - run it under the skill's recommended process manager for Node (PM2) with auto-restart on crash, expose a health-check endpoint that returns HTTP 200, and emit structured JSON logs; then verify each principle really holds.
evidence: Work dir real2_work/r112. Checked runtime: node v22.22.0, npm 10.9.4. Wrote server.js (http server with /health returning JSON+200 and structured JSON logging) and package.json. Installed PM2 7.1.1 locally into ./node_modules via npm --silent (no global/sudo). Started service under PM2 with PM2_HOME inside the work dir: pm2 start server.js --name r112 -> status online, pid 19121, restarts=0. PROCESS MANAGEMENT / RESTART-ON-CRASH principle verified: killed the worker with kill -9 19121; after ~3s PM2 reported status online, restart_time=1, new pid 19250 (auto-recovery). HEALTH CHECK principle verified: curl /health returned HTTP_CODE=200 with body {status:ok,...} both before the kill (pid 19121) and after the restart (pid 19250). LOG MANAGEMENT principle verified: pm2 out log file contains structured JSON lines, e.g. {level:info,msg:'server listening',port:3000,pid:19121} and {level:info,msg:'health check served',pid:19250}. Cleaned up with pm2 delete all and pm2 kill. Core deliverable - a server actually managed per the skill's principles with verified auto-restart, health check, and structured logging - exists and was verified. The skill is principles-only and names no bundled script/file, so nothing of the skill itself was missing.
